<description>
`-bytespersigop` is parsed as int64, stored as unsigned int, and multiplied by a transaction's sigop cost into the int32 sizes used by the mempool. Negative values wrap, values of 2^32 or more are truncated (4294967296 turns the sigop adjustment off), and large values overflow, so a debug build aborts on an `Assume`. The first commit refuses any value outside [0, 21474] at startup: up to 21474, a package of 25 transactions at the standard sigops limit still has an int32 size.

The second commit checks the sigops limit before a transaction is staged. A transaction that is otherwise standard can be far over that limit, and at 21474 one with about 100,000 sigops still overflows when staged. `mempool_sigoplimit.py` covers the range, a 25-transaction package at 21474, and that transaction.
</description>

Not sure this is a valid use-case, but the parsing is likely broken in this case anyway on this pull and master: It is parsed as i64, then assigned to u32, then used in a i32 calculation. Every step either truncates, wraps, or aborts. I'd say if this is fixed, it would be good to fix all of them.
[2026-10-15] c:6202412797 comment by fametrano (contributor):
Agreed, fixed in 7d37a758b3: `-bytespersigop` outside [0, 21474] is now refused at startup, so it is stored without wrapping or truncation. 21474 is the largest value at which a package of 25 transactions at the standard sigops limit keeps an int32 size. A bound of 134217 would cover one transaction, but a package of 5 then aborts a debug build. I kept the sigops check before staging as a second commit, because a single transaction far over the limit still overflows at 21474.
</new_statements>
